Dear Congresswoman Pressley,

How absolutely pathetic to watch you regurgitate the same tired talking points while adding your signature social justice buzzwords about "cruel, political, and unjust" decisions. Your decades of activism apparently didn't include courses in constitutional law, federalism, or original thought.

Let me help clarify what actually happened here, since constitutional law obviously wasn't covered in your community organizing background. The Supreme Court didn't "rob" anyone of anything – they allowed states to exercise their Tenth Amendment authority to decide how to spend their Medicaid dollars. You know, that pesky concept called federalism that you progressives have spent decades trying to destroy in favor of centralized government control.

Your concern for "patients & mothers" is particularly rich when basic reproductive responsibility costs about $1 per condom (or as little as 33 cents each when you buy a 12-pack). We're talking about approximately $12 per year for comprehensive birth control – less than you probably spend on a single organic smoothie in your gentrified district. Are you seriously suggesting women can't afford $12 annually for personal responsibility, or are you just so committed to government dependency that you can't imagine people managing their own healthcare without federal subsidies?

Here's what's really fascinating about your social justice healthcare rhetoric: you're demanding taxpayer funding for one specific organization while completely ignoring that organizations like PreBorn! operate entirely without government subsidies, providing free ultrasounds, counseling, and comprehensive support to women nationwide. There are also thousands of federally qualified health centers, community health centers, private practices, and faith-based organizations providing the exact same services you claim are being put "out of reach." But acknowledging these alternatives would undermine your entire victimhood narrative.

Your progressive defense of Planned Parenthood is particularly disturbing given your claims to fight systemic racism. You're championing an organization founded by Margaret Sanger specifically to control population growth in minority communities. The same Democratic Party that defended slavery, created Jim Crow laws, and founded Planned Parenthood to (in Sanger's own words) manage "undesirable" populations now claims to champion healthcare access. Your entire progressive platform is built on keeping minorities dependent on government programs instead of empowering them with economic freedom – it's the same plantation system with Black Lives Matter branding.

Speaking of "cruel" and "unjust," remember when your party guaranteed the Affordable Care Act would ensure "healthcare for all Americans"? Obama promised universal coverage, that premiums would go down by $2,500, and that "if you like your healthcare plan, you can keep it." Instead, up to 9.3 million people lost their coverage, premiums increased by 60% in the first four years, and PolitiFact named Obama's promise the "Lie of the Year." Your party guaranteed universal healthcare coverage through the ACA – so why are you still demanding special funding for one organization when you supposedly already achieved comprehensive coverage?

Your constitutional ignorance is particularly embarrassing for someone who took an oath of office. The federal government has zero enumerated power to fund healthcare organizations. That authority belongs to states under the Tenth Amendment. So your outrage about this "damning" ruling is actually directed at the Court for... upholding the Constitution you swore to defend. But I suppose constitutional fidelity interferes with your progressive agenda of federal control over everything.

Your claim about putting healthcare "out of reach for millions" is both factually false and deliberately inflammatory. Essential healthcare is available at over 1,400 federally qualified health centers, thousands of community health centers, private practices, and hospital systems nationwide. Suggesting that one politically-connected organization is essential for millions of Americans is either deliberate misinformation or stunning ignorance of healthcare infrastructure.

Perhaps between your social justice activism and your progressive grandstanding, you could explain why taxpayers should fund your preferred political organization when thousands of other healthcare providers exist? Or why we need special funding for one organization when your party guaranteed universal healthcare coverage? Or why you're violating your constitutional oath to defend federalism? Or why you can't formulate an original thought instead of copying nine other Democrats who already embarrassed themselves with identical talking points?
